stem: Ruthenium and osmium are transition metals below iron in Group 8 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Two different complex ions, **X** and **Y**, can form when anhydrous $\text{RuCl}_3$ reacts with water under certain conditions.

**X** and **Y** have octahedral geometry.

Aqueous samples of **X** and **Y** react separately with an excess of $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$. Different amounts of $\text{AgCl}$ are precipitated:

- 1 mole of complex ion **X** produces 2 moles of $\text{AgCl}$
- 1 mole of complex ion **Y** produces 1 mole of $\text{AgCl}$.

(b)(i)
parts.text: Suggest how pyrazine is able to bond to two separate ruthenium ions.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Pyrazine is an aromatic compound. The bonding and structure of pyrazine is similar to that of benzene.

Describe and explain the shape of pyrazine.

In your answer, include:

- the hybridisation of the nitrogen and carbon atoms
- how orbital overlap forms $\pi$ bonds between the atoms in the ring.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Predict the number of peaks seen in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of pyrazine.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The overall charge of the ruthenium complex in Fig. 4.1 is 5+.

Deduce the possible oxidation states of the two ruthenium ions in the complex.
